messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/generate via router (eu-west-1). p99=6.3s, p95=1.2s, streaming stalls increasing. Auto-page to oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032-45. Paged: sasha. Priority: P1.

sasha: acked. joining. seeing the p99 surge in the dashboard too. tagging eng-sre.

leo: on it, joining call. initial hypothesis: router routing policy abnormal, some requests stuck behind a tiny subset of upstreams.

maya: i can repro a few streaming stalls locally when we route to host-group A. looks like hot partitioning on lb-targets.

dan: logs show a batch of 502/504 from a subset of backend nodes starting at 1750004200. maybe a policy that accidentally pins traffic?

leo: confirming: rule "region-aware-prefer" has a fallback weight that ended up with 90% -> host-group-A due to new rollout. policy change earlier today by tim.

tim: i rolled a traffic-weight change at 1750004100 to favor eu-west-1-primary, intended 60/40, looks like a typo set to 99/1. investigating why rollout system accepted it.

maya: hot partition on host-group-A: connection queue depth rising, KV cache evictions, stream stalls. If we keep routing there p99 will stay high.

leo: mitigation plan: 1) rollback traffic-weight to previous stable (60/40) 2) temporarily mark host-group-A as drain/avoid in router 3) scale router frontend + lb targets 4) monitor p99 and streaming stalls.

sasha: proceeding with rollback. @tim can you confirm the exact previous weight?

tim: previous was 60/40, confirmed. rolling back now. command: `routerctl set-weight region-aware-prefer eu-west-1-primary=60 eu-west-1-secondary=40 --change-author=tim`

infra-bot: deploy job started: routerctl-change-1750004399.

leo: while rollback runs, mark host-group-A unhealthy in balancer so new requests avoid it: `lbctl set-target-health host-group-A unhealthy --reason="mitigating-tail-latency"`

maya: doing that now... done. health check draining started.

dan: scaling router frontend replicas from 4 -> 8 as precaution: `kubectl scale deploy/router-frontend -n prod --replicas=8`

infra-bot: routerctl-change-1750004399 succeeded. traffic weights updated.

sasha: p99 just dropped from 6.3s -> 1.4s in the next 90s. p95 stable. streaming stalls reduced but still seeing occasional stalls (likely from in-flight requests hitting drained nodes).

leo: next step: remove any pinned routing keys that might still be sticky to host-group-A. running backfill to redistribute sticky session keys.

maya: backfill started: `routerctl redistribute-sticky-keys --target=eu-west-1-secondary --concurrency=50`

oliver: CS here. any known customer impact? We have a customer on a demo in EU complaining about slow responses. Do we need to open a support ticket?

sasha: impact window ~1750004100-1750004400. approx 4% of requests were at p99 >5s. no data corruption, mainly increased latency and streaming stalls. recommend proactive outreach to top EU customers.

tim: i'll open a short postmortem note and tag the release that changed the weights. need to fix rollout validation to block >15% delta without a canary.

leo: agreed. immediate action items: (a) revert rollout validation to prevent accidental 99/1 weight (owner: tim) (b) add a guard in routerctl to require canary for weight deltas >20% (owner: eng-platform) (c) add metric alert for sudden concentrated target weight shifts (owner: eng-sre).

dan: i've added a temporary alert on our dashboards for host-group imbalance.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation in place. p99 reduced to ~1.2s. Streaming stalls decreased. Status: under control.

oliver: sending a short customer message now: "We're aware of latency issues in EU region earlier today, root cause was a misapplied routing weight change. Mitigation rolled out and latency restored. We're following up with a timeline and prevention plan."

sasha: handoff: i'll stay on until 1750005400 and then hand to leo for the follow-up and postmortem. pls add any extra notes.

leo: thanks — i'll own the post-incident review and the follow-up tasks. collecting logs and request samples now. if anyone has high-priority request IDs to include, DM me.

tim: i'll submit a PR to add rollout validation tests and a small UI guard by EOD.

infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: tail-latency mitigation successful. incident closed for now; monitor for 2 hours.

sasha: closing thread. Thanks all for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
